groups.note: Malayalam working translation, AI-assisted and not yet independently reviewed. Original Codex draft (2026), based directly on the project’s normalized Sanskrit transcription of Sylvain Lévi’s 1925 edition, not attributed to any named scholar. Upacāra is a transferred designation, not an assertion of a substantial self. All mappings are phrase-level, not word-for-word or morphological analyses.
The Sanskrit relative-correlative yaḥ/asau is rendered idiomatically as a resumed statement. Sanskrit token order and identity remain unchanged.
Vijñapti is retained as വിജ്ഞപ്തി; it is not silently equated with vijñāna (വിജ്ഞാനം).
Bīja is a causal-dispositional metaphor. No permanent receptacle is asserted by the wording.

groups.text: അതിന്റെ ഉപാദിയും സ്ഥാനവും വിജ്ഞപ്തിയും വ്യക്തമായി അറിയപ്പെടാത്തവയാണ്;
groups.note: UNREVIEWED / UNCERTAIN: the internal scope of asaṃviditaka-upādi-sthāna-vijñaptika is unresolved. This provisional reading lists upādi, location and presentation as not distinctly known; an alternative attaches the unperceived quality to presentation of appropriation and location. Upādi is retained without fixing its exact sense. No independent lexical attestation is claimed.

groups.text: എപ്പോഴും സ്പർശം, മനസ്കാരം, വേദന, സംജ്ഞ, ചേതന എന്നിവയോടുകൂടിയതുമാണ്.
groups.note: Vit is provisionally rendered as feeling (വേദന), in light of vedanā in v4. Manaskāra, saṃjñā and cetanā remain technical factors; cetanā is volition, not consciousness in general.
Vedanā means feeling tone, not pain alone. Upekṣā here is neutral feeling, not an independently asserted meditative achievement.

groups.text: അതാകട്ടെ ക്ലേശാവരണമില്ലാത്തതും കുശലമോ അകുശലമോ ആയി നിർണയിക്കപ്പെടാത്തതുമാണ്.
groups.note: Anivṛta/avyākṛta are rendered descriptively: unobscured by afflictions and ethically indeterminate. The edition reading is retained.
Vyāvṛtti is rendered as നിവൃത്തി; its doctrinal interpretation at arhatship remains open. It is not silently identified with parāvṛtti in v29.

groups.text: അതിനെത്തന്നെ ആലംബനമാക്കുന്ന, മനസ് എന്നു പേരുള്ള, മനനസ്വഭാവമായ വിജ്ഞാനം.
groups.note: The subject of the preceding Malayalam clause follows here, matching the Sanskrit movement. Manas is distinguished from manovijñāna in v16.

groups.text: ആവൃതവും അവ്യാകൃതവുമായ നാല് ക്ലേശങ്ങളോടുകൂടിയാണ് അത് എപ്പോഴും:
groups.note: Nivṛta and avyākṛta qualify the four kleśas in the Sanskrit instrumental phrase. The draft does not turn ethical indeterminacy into an absence of affliction.

groups.text: ആത്മദൃഷ്ടി, ആത്മമോഹം, ആത്മമാനം, ആത്മസ്നേഹം എന്നു പേരുള്ളവയോട്.
ഏതു ഭൂമിയിൽ ജനിക്കുന്നുവോ, അതിനൊത്ത മറ്റു സ്പർശാദികളോടും കൂടിയതാണ്;
groups.note: ഭൂമി renders the contextual sphere implied by yatrajaḥ. The Sanskrit does not name a particular realm. The association continues from v6.
The absent referent is the afflicted manas just described, not all awareness of an arhat.
Advayā here means neither wholesome nor unwholesome; it is not translated as the later subject-object nonduality.

groups.text: അതുപോലെ ക്ലേശങ്ങളോടും ഉപക്ലേശങ്ങളോടും; മൂന്നു വിധ വേദനകളോടുകൂടിയതുമാണ്.
groups.note: Three kinds of feeling are a classification, not a claim that all three occur simultaneously.

groups.text: ഛന്ദം, അധിമോക്ഷം, സ്മൃതി എന്നിവയും സമാധി, ധീ എന്നിവയും വിഷയനിയതങ്ങളാണ്.
groups.note: Contextual study glosses: chanda = intention/desire to act; adhimokṣa = resolve; smṛti = recollection/mindfulness; samādhi = concentration; dhī = discernment. Technical Malayalam usage needs specialist review.

groups.text: തുടർന്ന് വിശ്വാസവും ധാർമ്മിക ലജ്ജയും അന്യരെ മാനിച്ചുള്ള സംകോചവും;
groups.note: Hrī and apatrapā are provisionally distinguished as moral shame and restraint with regard for others. These are draft renderings, not quotations from a Malayalam Buddhist lexicon. The wholesome list continues in v11.
The Sanskrit abbreviates the three roots as alobhādi trayam. The text does not insert the other two roots; their familiar expansion (non-hatred and non-delusion) belongs in commentary.
Praśrabdhi is retained as പ്രശ്രബ്ധി (ease/pliancy of body and mind). Sāpramādikā is read sa-apramādikā, with heedfulness, not with negligence.
Dṛṣṭi is afflictive in this list; the translation does not condemn every view indiscriminately.
Mrakṣa and pradāśa are provisional contextual renderings (concealment of faults and hostility). Their technical Malayalam equivalents need review.
Follows the declared source emendation vihiṃsā + ahrīḥ: harmfulness and shamelessness. It must not be read as ahiṃsā and hrī.

groups.text: അന്യരെക്കുറിച്ചുള്ള ധാർമ്മിക കരുതലില്ലായ്മ, മനസ്സിന്റെ മന്ദത, അസ്വസ്ഥത,
groups.note: Uddhavaḥ is the retained edition reading; അസ്വസ്ഥത is provisional. Atrapā is distinguished from ahrīḥ through relation to others, pending review.
Vitarka and vicāra are retained as technical terms. Applied/initial and sustained examination are possible explanatory glosses, not established here as uniquely correct.
The two pairs are regret/sleep and vitarka/vicāra. Dvidhā is kept open as a twofold status; the draft does not impose one classification scheme or label all four intrinsically unwholesome.

groups.text: മനോവിജ്ഞാനം എല്ലായ്പ്പോഴും ഉദിക്കുന്നു—അസംജ്ഞികാവസ്ഥയും രണ്ടു സമാപത്തികളും ഒഴികെ;
groups.note: MERGED ADJACENT BLOCKS 1–2: sarvadāsaṃjñikāt contains both “always” and the first exception, governed by ṛte in the next block. One phrase mapping avoids falsely separating the exception from its governor. The Sanskrit layout remains unchanged. The two attainments are not individually named in this verse.
Acittaka restricts the relevant sleep/fainting states to those without active cognition. The draft does not say all sleep or fainting lacks cognition.
Vikalpa is retained as വികൽപം: discriminative/conceptual construction, not merely deliberate fantasy.
The denial concerns what is constructed as constructed. No additional thesis denying every possible sense of reality is inserted.

UNREVIEWED / UNCERTAIN: Lévi’s nominative-looking pariṇāmas with yāti is retained in the Sanskrit. The Malayalam gives a provisional contextual reading, “passes through various transformations,” without silently correcting the source to an accusative form. Philological review is required.
Mutual influence is retained without specifying every causal direction or identifying each relatum; the Sanskrit here does not do so.
Grāhadvaya is retained as ദ്വയഗ്രഹണം. Subject/object or grasper/grasped is the contextual explanation, not two literal grasping acts.

UNREVIEWED / UNCERTAIN: final tat has no securely assigned referent in this draft. The Malayalam uses the connective അങ്ങനെ without asserting a separate entity or precise one-token correspondence; this is an interpretive concession requiring review. Token coverage alone does not prove an exact rendering of that pronoun.
Sa refers to the parikalpita nature as posited. The denial is not expanded here into a claim about all dependent functioning.

MERGED ADJACENT BLOCKS 2–3: niṣpannas tasya and the following absence clause form one predication whose natural Malayalam order is reversed. “The earlier” is kept as മുൻപറഞ്ഞത്; context points to the parikalpita of v20. This asserts absence of that imagined nature in the dependent, not disappearance of dependent functioning.
The first sa is provisionally understood as the perfected nature, following v21; the Malayalam retains the pronoun.

UNREVIEWED / UNCERTAIN: asmin and sa are deliberately retained as “this” and “that.” The common contextual reading takes this as perfected and that as dependent, but the translation does not hide the pronoun-resolution question.

groups.text: അടുത്തത് സ്വയം ഉദിക്കുന്നതല്ലാത്തതിനാൽ നിഃസ്വഭാവമാണ്; മറ്റൊരു നിഃസ്വഭാവതയുമുണ്ട്—
groups.note: MERGED ADJACENT BLOCKS 2–3: etasya belongs with the preceding denial of self-arising. “Is without own-nature” is supplied for the second nature from the preceding predication. The final phrase preserves the further aparā niḥsvabhāvatā transition into v25. Whether this introduces the third mode rather than merely restates the second must be reviewed; the earlier English annotation should not decide it silently.
Paramārtha is retained as പരമാർത്ഥം; “ultimate reality” and “highest meaning” are not adjudicated here. This continues the compressed v24–25 argument.
Yataḥ is absorbed into the explanatory sequence completed by the following because-clause, rather than assigned an isolated Malayalam word. Tathatā is retained as തഥത.
Always being thus explains tathatā; it does not assert an eternal personal consciousness.
Anuśaya is retained as അനുശയം: a latent tendency, not merely an explicit belief.

കരുതിയാലും (“even if one thinks”) is an idiomatic connective supplied across the quotation and api. This is a phrase mapping, not an assertion that a separate Sanskrit word means “thinks.” Upalambha is rendered as grasping hold.
UNREVIEWED / UNCERTAIN: follows Lévi’s yadā-ālambanam and vijñānam without inserting the modern tu or substituting jñānam. The scope of non-apprehension remains doctrinally contested.
Retains vijñānamātratva as വിജ്ഞാനമാത്രത, distinct from വിജ്ഞപ്തിമാത്രത elsewhere. Do not normalize the two expressions into one witness reading.

UNREVIEWED / UNCERTAIN: Malayalam provisionally renders tad-agrahāt as “because [it/one] does not grasp it,” without resolving the implicit agent or the pronoun’s referent. The relation to the absence of a grasped object requires philological/doctrinal review; no unconsciousness claim is added.
Acitta is rendered literally as ചിത്തരഹിതം, but is immediately coordinated with knowledge. It must not be read uncritically as unconscious stupor; the technical interpretation remains open.
Dauṣṭhulya is retained as ദൗഷ്ഠുല്യം (encumbering unfitness). The text says removal is twofold without naming two obstructions; those identifications belong in commentary.
Dhruva is retained as ധ്രുവം. Its doctrinal relation to impermanence is not settled by this draft.
Kāya is carried contextually from vimuktikāya into dharmākhya. The Malayalam ധർമ്മകായം is thus a phrase-level interpretation, not an extra Sanskrit word or a new morphological segment.
